intent: Represents a single client command as it flows through Bedrock's prePeek/peek/process/postProcess pipeline, tracking plugin ownership, HTTPS sub-requests, per-phase timing, timeout policy, and crash-diagnostic state.

objects.name: BedrockCommand
objects.role: extends SQLiteCommand; the per-request unit of work with virtual peek/process hooks for plugins to override

objects.name: BedrockCommand::TIMING_INFO
objects.role: phase labels for timing samples, including BLOCKING_* variants for the blocking commit thread

objects.name: BedrockCommand::STAGE
objects.role: which pipeline stage reset() is being called for

objects.name: BedrockCommand::GrowOnlyList<T>
objects.role: append-only wrapper around list<T> (no erase); holds httpsRequests so iterators stay stable

objects.name: BedrockCommand::CrashMap
objects.role: subset of request name/value pairs used to fingerprint commands that may have caused a crash

misfits.why: a generic, command-agnostic container template with no dependency on BedrockCommand, defined inline inside it
special-cases a 'returnValueList' suffix documented in-code as a hack to support one legacy plugin format (Auth's old Get), inside the generic base command class
a sizeable timing-metrics/logging routine (per-phase totals, upstream-value promotion, a long SINFO composition) bundled into the command class itself rather than a separate metrics helper

location_fit.note: top-level, consistent with other core command-pipeline types (BedrockCore, BedrockServer)

naming_quality.note: consistent `_` on non-public members; TIMING_INFO is a plain unscoped enum sitting beside STAGE, which correctly uses enum class

intent: Runs a BedrockCommand's prePeek/peek/process/postProcess lifecycle against a specific SQLite db and transaction, translating thrown exceptions into HTTP-style response codes.

objects.name: BedrockCore
objects.role: extends SQLiteCore; executes a command's lifecycle methods against _db, handling timeouts/aborts/exceptions

objects.name: BedrockCore::RESULT
objects.role: outcome codes from peekCommand/processCommand (COMPLETE, SHOULD_PROCESS, NEEDS_COMMIT, NO_COMMIT_REQUIRED, SERVER_NOT_LEADING)

objects.name: BedrockCore::AutoTimer
objects.role: records one timing entry into command->timingInfo spanning its own lifetime

objects.name: AutoScopeRewrite
objects.role: RAII enable/disable of SQLite's query-rewrite hook for one process() call

misfits.why: defined at file scope in BedrockCore.cpp without `static` or an anonymous namespace, so its file-local intent relies on convention rather than being enforced

location_fit.note: fits; sits at the repo root as the execution engine beside BedrockCommand and BedrockServer

naming_quality.note: consistent; `_server` follows the `_` convention for private members

intent: Process entry point for the Bedrock server binary: parses arguments, applies defaults, handles one-shot maintenance flags, loads plugins, initializes SQLite/SSL/signal handling, and runs the main poll loop.

objects.name: main
objects.role: entry point; startup/shutdown sequencing and the main prePoll/poll/postPoll loop

objects.name: RetrySystem
objects.role: runs a shell command via system(), retrying up to 3 times with a 5s backoff, fatal SERROR if it never succeeds

objects.name: VacuumDB
objects.role: shells out to `sqlite3 <db> 'VACUUM;'` via RetrySystem

objects.name: BackupDB
objects.role: copies the db file plus its -wal/-shm sidecars into BACKUP_DIR

objects.name: loadPlugins
objects.role: registers built-in plugins by name and dlopen/dlsym's any plugin named in -plugins that isn't built in

misfits.why: shell out to the external `sqlite3` binary and hardcode a `/var/tmp/` backup path inside the process entry point; BACKUP_DIR is the only path in this file not configurable via args like everything else here
a self-contained dlopen/dlsym plugin-registration subsystem implemented as a free function in main.cpp

naming_quality.note: RetrySystem/VacuumDB/BackupDB use PascalCase while loadPlugins uses camelCase, for free functions at the same file scope

intent: A BedrockCommandQueue subclass, used for the blocking commit thread's queue, that adds per-identifier and per-command-name sliding-window rate limiting, rejecting commands whose key has spent too much recent time on the queue.

objects.name: BedrockBlockingCommandQueue
objects.role: extends BedrockCommandQueue; adds rate-limit checks to push()/_dequeue() plus configuration and status reporting

objects.name: BedrockBlockingCommandQueue::RecentlyFinishedCommand
objects.role: one timed sample (finishTime, elapsedTime) in the sliding window

objects.name: BedrockBlockingCommandQueue::RecentlyFinishedCommandList
objects.role: deque<RecentlyFinishedCommand>, oldest first

objects.name: BedrockBlockingCommandQueue::IdentifierState
objects.role: one tracked key's mutex, recent-sample deque, and block-until deadline

objects.name: BedrockBlockingCommandQueue::StateMap
objects.role: mutex-guarded unordered_map<string, shared_ptr<IdentifierState>>; one instance each for identifiers and command names

misfits.why: a generic string-keyed sliding-window rate limiter with no dependency on BedrockCommand, implemented as private nested machinery of a command-queue subclass
misfits.suggested_home: libstuff, as a general-purpose rate limiter

name_fit.note: 'Blocking' refers to the blocking commit thread's queue, which this class serves; the rate-limiting role isn't in the name

location_fit.note: fits; sits beside its base class BedrockCommandQueue

naming_quality.note: consistent `_` prefix on private members; Identifier vs Command dimensions named distinctly with no confusable aliasing

intent: A thread-safe, time-ordered queue of BedrockCommands keyed by scheduled time and timeout, from which worker threads block-and-wait for the next command that is either already timed out or due to run.

objects.name: BedrockCommandQueue
objects.role: push/get/_dequeue, the timed-out-vs-scheduled ordering rule, and empty/size/clear/getAll queries

objects.name: BedrockCommandQueue::timeout_error
objects.role: thrown by get() when its wait window elapses with nothing available

objects.name: BedrockCommandQueue::ItemTimeoutPair
objects.role: pairs a queued command with its timeout for the parallel _lookupByTimeout index

naming_quality.note: Timeout and Scheduled are both bare uint64_t typedefs, mutually assignable with nothing at the type level stopping one being passed where the other is expected
